hints: Focus on what happens to the OH group of the alcohol in each of these three very different reaction types.
Remember that esterification joins an acid and an alcohol, while HBr replaces OH with Br, so track where the H and OH end up.
Now think about dehydration over hot aluminium oxide, and check if all three reactions split out H and OH to make a small molecule.
walkthrough:
**Recall reaction 1, esterification**

Great start, let's look at alcohol plus carboxylic acid. This is a condensation reaction where water is split out to join the two molecules.

$$\text{R-OH} + \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOR} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Recall reaction 2, substitution with HBr**

Next, alcohol with concentrated HBr gives a bromoalkane. The OH is replaced by Br, and the H from HBr joins OH to form water.

$$\text{R-OH} + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{R-Br} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Recall reaction 3, dehydration over Al2O3**

Finally, hot $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is a dehydrating agent. It removes H and OH from adjacent carbons to form an alkene plus water.

$$\text{R-CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{R-CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Combine the conclusion**

All three reactions produce water as one product. So the correct combination is 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct. All three give water. Reaction 1 is esterification, reaction 2 is nucleophilic substitution to form RBr, and reaction 3 is elimination (dehydration) to form an alkene. In each case $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is formed.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and 2 and leaves out 3. Students sometimes forget that passing vapour over heated $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is called dehydration precisely because water is eliminated to give the alkene.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only 2 and 3 and leaves out 1. Students sometimes think esterification only makes the ester, forgetting it is a condensation reaction where $\text{CH}_3\text{COOR}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ are both formed.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and leaves out 2 and 3. Students sometimes confuse reaction with HBr (which does make water) with free radical substitution of alkanes, or confuse $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ dehydration with dehydrogenation using other catalysts.
